newsitem.title: DENMARK: Carlsberg reports H1 sales, profits up.
newsitem.headline: Carlsberg reports H1 sales, profits up.

text.p: Danish brewer Carlsberg on Tuesday reported first half 1996/1997 sales and profits up on the same period a year earlier despite a shrinking domestic beer market and uncertainty about the sale of its Carlsberg-Tetley operation to Britain's Bass.

The report, for the six months to March 31, 1997, logged pre-tax profit up to 870 million crowns ($132.2 million) from 741 million the year before and turnover up to 9.21 billion crowns from 8.54 billion.
Analysts had on average forecast pre-tax profit of 812 million crowns and turnover of 8.99 billion.
Carlsberg said that much of the rise in turnover came from the stronger British pound and an increased stake in Norwegian brewer Falcon, to 50 percent from 30 percent.
It said that Carslberg-Tetley, which it jointly owns with Bass, had a first-half result similar to that of the year before but it gave no figure.
